verification_level: FAST plus BATCH; five repairs (one out-of-bounds read in the OID module, one out-of-bounds pointer formation in the control-message walk, one past-the-terminator read for a NUL list separator, one missing panic boundary on the printf engine's C entry points, and one zero-length pointer-arithmetic case), five focused tests plus two buffer tests, the full library suite serially and with four threads, clippy and fmt, and the Phase 2, Phase 4 and Phase 6 courts against a distribution shell rebuilt from this exact source. Miri/ASan and Loom are NOT_RUN.
scope: Per-file contract audit of the BIO printf engine and its non-variadic surface, the descriptor retry classifiers, the libc/BIO operating-system surface (including the CMSG walk), the BUF_MEM buffer owner, OPENSSL_INIT_SETTINGS, the oid_section module and CONF_parse_list. All eight entries were the head of REMAINING-AUDIT.txt; none was deferred. buffer.rs is a shared buffer owner: only BUF_reverse and a test module were touched, so the OwnedData ownership mechanism and OB-1/OB-4 evidence are unchanged.

defects.class: out-of-bounds backward read in the OID module's long-name trim
defects.description: do_create's `long name, oid` shape walks the long-name half backwards over whitespace with the authority's floor `p == ln`. When the whole half is whitespace, `ln` (the first non-whitespace byte) is the comma itself, so the floor is unreachable and `p.sub(1)` steps before `value`; the loop then reads `*p` outside the allocation. The C authority has the same defect, but §17 forbids reproducing it. A quoted oid_section value can carry the leading whitespace the CONF reader otherwise strips. The guard now refuses the all-whitespace half, which is the authority's observed result whenever the byte before the value is not whitespace.
defects.divergence: For a value whose long-name half is entirely whitespace the candidate returns 0 (module initialiser raises ASN_MOID_38); the authority reads before its buffer and in practice also fails. Every well-formed shape is unchanged.

defects.description: The walk formed `next = prev + CMSG_ALIGN(prev_len)` and then tested `next + sizeof(cmsghdr) > end`. On the ordinary final record `next == end`, so the test itself created a pointer 16 bytes past the allocation — undefined behaviour in Rust on every completed control-message walk, although it was never dereferenced. CMSG_ALIGN(prev_len) also used unchecked `+ 7`, so a corrupted cmsg_len panicked under the crate's overflow checks. The walk now compares offsets computed from `prev.offset_from(ctl)`, uses a checked alignment round-up, and forms `next` only after proving the record and its header fit inside `[ctl, ctl + len)`.
defects.divergence: No change for any well-formed record set; the record count and returned pointers are identical. A cmsg_len that cannot fit ends the walk instead of panicking.

defects.class: past-the-terminator read when the list separator is NUL
defects.description: `strchr(s, 0)` returns the terminator rather than NULL. With sep == 0 the walk treated that as a separator, delivered the whole string as one element, set `lstart = p + 1`, and dereferenced one byte past the NUL on the next iteration. The authority has the same loop and the same UB. A terminator match is now normalised to "no separator" (a NUL cannot delimit a C string), so the walk stops after delivering the single element; for every non-zero sep the normalisation is unreachable.
defects.divergence: sep == 0 now delivers one element (or one empty element for an empty list) and returns 1 without reading past the string; sep != 0 is bit-identical.

defects.class: missing panic boundary on the C-ABI printf entry points
defects.description: openssl_rs_dopr_snprintf and openssl_rs_dopr_vprintf are `extern "C"` entry points called from bio_variadic.c and were the only ones in this family without guard_ffi. The engine performs width/precision arithmetic under `overflow-checks = true`, and a conforming call such as BIO_snprintf(b, n, "%*d", INT_MIN, 1) overflows `-min`, panicking in release and aborting when the panic cannot cross the C frame; a precision near INT_MAX also overflows the padding sum. Both entry points are now wrapped in guard_ffi(-1, ...), so such a panic becomes the documented failure value.
defects.divergence: Only panic paths change (abort -> -1). Every non-panicking format is unchanged; bytes written before a failure remain written, as in the authority's own failure shape.

defects.description: With size == 0 the implementation formed `out.add(size.wrapping_sub(1))`, an offset of usize::MAX and therefore an out-of-bounds pointer in Rust, even though the loop body never ran. The documented contract (out points to size writable bytes) is satisfied by a zero-length call, so this was reachable by a conforming C caller. A size == 0 early return now preserves the no-op behaviour without any pointer arithmetic. In-crate callers guard their lengths, so no call site changes.
defects.divergence: None: the authority writes nothing for size 0 as well.

deferred: ASan: the repaired paths are offset/length logic in this crate; the cmsg and OID changes remove out-of-bounds reads/pointers but no sanitizer build was run (BOUNDARY).

Miri: unavailable on the pinned 1.98.1 stable toolchain ('the miri component is not available'); the asn1 and cmsg bounds changes are the strongest Miri candidates and are recorded as NOT_RUN (BOUNDARY).
Loom: no concurrency or refcount change.
Dependency-graph regeneration: no shared mechanism's contract was edited; buffer.rs ownership was not touched.
FRF and SEAL; constant-time review (no secret-dependent control-flow claim).
not_discharged: All eight files are audited, not SAFETY_DISCHARGED.
The OID module's refusal of an all-whitespace long-name half is a deliberate safety divergence from the authority's out-of-bounds read, not a new compatibility result.

cmsg_nxthdr's third condition (the next record's own cmsg_len must be at least a header) is retained as a safety improvement over glibc's __cmsg_nxthdr, which returns a short record; it only changes malformed-buffer walks.
CONF_parse_list's NULL-list and NULL-callback answers remain the recorded total-by-policy divergences from the authority's fault.

BUF_MEM_free releases the BUF_MEM struct with CRYPTO_clear_free of its size where the authority uses CRYPTO_free; retained as a cleansing improvement, with the data block's cleansing release unchanged.
CONF_get1_default_config_file's no-OPENSSL_CONF branch returns the empty string rather than the authority's forensic OPENSSLDIR (OBL-CONF-DEFAULT-CONFIG-FILE, Phase 16).
retained_obligations: print_engine::dopr requires format NUL-terminated and, with a fixed sink, fixed writable for maxlen; `%s`/`%n` argument types are the caller's varargs contract. The entry points now also require a live BIO (vprintf).
fmtstr's `%s` scan is bounded by the precision when one is given, so a caller satisfying C's printf contract (NUL-terminated for an unbounded %s, or at least `precision` bytes) is safe.
cmsg_firsthdr/cmsg_nxthdr require a live Msghdr whose msg_control is readable for msg_controllen bytes, and prev must be a record from the same buffer.
cmsg_hdr/cmsg_set_hdr/cmsg_data operate on byte pointers with unaligned access; the caller must establish the record lies inside the control buffer.
CONF_parse_list requires a NUL-terminated list (or NULL) and a callback accepting (NULL-or-string, len); sep must be a separator byte, and sep == 0 is now total.
BUF_MEM_grow/grow_clean require NULL or a live BUF_MEM whose data block has capacity max; BUF_reverse requires out writable for size bytes and a non-overlapping input.
do_create requires NUL-terminated value and name (name non-NULL); OBJ_create copies its arguments before the lntmp owner is released.
OPENSSL_INIT_set_config_* require a live settings object from OPENSSL_INIT_new; the libc malloc/strdup/free pair is the authority's own seam and must stay paired.
documentation_corrections: BUF_reverse's doc now states that size == 0 returns before any pointer arithmetic instead of claiming out - 1 is well defined.
cmsg_nxthdr's doc now names the offset-based bounds test and the retained third condition honestly.
The OID module's backward-walk comment records that the authority's floor is unreachable for an all-whitespace long-name half.
CONF_parse_list's separator comment records that a NUL separator matches the terminator in strchr, which the authority mishandles.
shared_boundary_files: src/runtime/buffer.rs: BUF_reverse and a test module only; the OwnedData cleansing owner (OB-1/OwnedBlock-style) and the BUF_MEM public layout were not modified, so OB-1/OB-4 evidence remains bound to its existing source.
unsafe_operations_introduced: src/runtime/bio/sys.rs:540: prev.offset_from(ctl), after the contract establishes both derive from one control buffer.
src/runtime/conf/modparse.rs:143: one `*p` terminator read after strchr, inside the existing allocation.
unsafe_operations_removed: src/runtime/buffer.rs:335/350: out.add(size.wrapping_sub(1)) for the size == 0 case.
src/runtime/bio/sys.rs:534/540: prev.add(cmsg_align(prev_len)) and next.add(size_of::<Cmsghdr>()) as the bounds test; the latter was out of bounds at the final record.
src/runtime/confmod/asn1.rs:205: the p.sub(1) step that could leave the allocation is now unreachable.
secret_bearing_buffers: print_engine writes caller data into caller-owned or growing buffers and stores nothing; `%n` writes through the caller's pointer. No secret handling claim.
buffer.rs cleanses the BUF_MEM data block on release (CRYPTO_clear_free / CRYPTO_secure_clear_free) including the secure-heap branch; BUF_reverse touches caller buffers in place and stores nothing.
conf/modparse duplicates environment/default paths through OwnedStr and makes no secret claim.
confmod/asn1 copies the long name into an OPENSSL_malloc block released unconditionally after OBJ_create; OID names are public.
conf/init_settings uses libc malloc/strdup/free for a settings object that may predate CRYPTO_set_mem_functions; it holds filenames/appnames, not key material.

boundary_control.reason: The asn1 control drives the repaired floor directly; the sys control gives a record whose cmsg_len is usize::MAX, which the old code either aligned with an overflowing `+ 7` or turned into an out-of-bounds pointer; the modparse control drives sep == 0 on a non-empty and an empty list; the buffer controls pin the zero-length no-op and the ordinary copy/in-place reversal. The pre-existing bss_dgram::tests::cmsg_records_walk_in_order walks a two-record buffer to the exact end-of-buffer path that the old bounds test made UB, so it is the functional control for M75-D2. The Phase 2/4/6 courts below re-executed the affected surfaces against the rebuilt candidate. No sanitizer or Miri control was run (NOT_RUN).
